summary: Ben Zoma teaches who is truly wise, strong, rich and honored: one who learns from everyone, controls his yetzer hara, is happy with what he has, and honors other people.

chunks.en: Ben Zoma says:
Who is wise?
One who learns from every person,
as it says (Tehillim 119): From all my teachers
I became wise, because Your laws are what I talk about.
Who is strong?
One who controls his yetzer hara,
as it says (Mishlei 16): Better is one who is slow to anger
than a strong man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city.
Who is rich?
One who is happy with his share,
as it says (Tehillim 128): The work of your hands
when you eat it, you are fortunate and it is good for you.
You are fortunate in this world,
and it is good for you
in the World to Come.
Who is honored?
One who honors people,
as it says (Shmuel I 2): For
those who honor Me I will honor, and those who look down on Me will be made small.

summary: Ben Azzai teaches to run to do even a small mitzvah and to run away from aveiros, because one mitzvah leads to another and one aveirah leads to another.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says:
Run to do a light mitzvah just as you would a heavy one,
and run away from aveirah.
Because a mitzvah pulls along another mitzvah,
and an aveirah pulls along another aveirah.
Because the reward of a mitzvah
is a mitzvah, and the payment for an aveirah is an aveirah.

summary: Ben Azzai teaches not to look down on any person or on anything, because every person has his time and every thing has its place.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do not look down on any person,
and do not push away anything as impossible,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה
chunks.en: because there is no person who does not have his moment,

chunks.he: וְאֵין לְךָ דָבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם:
chunks.en: and there is no thing that does not have its place.

summary: Rabbi Levitas teaches to be very humble. Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka warns that one who makes Hashem's Name disgraced in secret is punished in public, whether he did it by accident or on purpose.

chunks.en: Rabbi Levitas of Yavneh says:
Be very, very humble,
because what waits for a person in the end is worms.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
Whoever disgraces the Name of Heaven in secret,
they punish him in public.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג וְאֶחָד מֵזִיד בְּחִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם:
chunks.en: Whether by accident or on purpose, it is the same when it comes to disgracing Hashem's Name.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches that one who learns in order to teach and to do gets help to do it all. Rabbi Tzadok warns not to use the Torah to make yourself great or to earn money.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael his son says:
One who learns Torah in order to teach,
they help him to learn and to teach.
And one who learns in order to do,

chunks.he: מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמֹד וּלְלַמֵּד לִשְׁמֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת.
chunks.en: they help him to learn, to teach, to guard and to do.
Rabbi Tzadok says:
Do not make the words of Torah a crown to make yourself great with,
and not an ax to dig with.
chunks.explain: Do not use the Torah as a tool to earn money.

chunks.en: And so Hillel used to say:
And one who uses the crown of Torah for himself
passes away. So you learned:
whoever gets benefit from words of Torah
takes away his life from the world.

summary: Rabbi Yosi teaches that one who honors the Torah will be honored by people, and one who disgraces the Torah will be disgraced by people.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says:
Whoever honors the Torah,
he himself will be honored by people.
And whoever disgraces the Torah,
he himself will be disgraced by people.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches that a judge who avoids judging when he can keeps away from many problems, but one who rushes to rule is foolish, wicked and proud.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael his son says:
One who holds himself back from judging,
chunks.explain: He tries to make peace between people instead.

chunks.he: פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ אֵיבָה וְגָזֵל וּשְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא.
chunks.en: removes from himself hatred, stealing, and a false oath.
And one who is too sure of himself when he rules,

words.en: and the one who is proud

chunks.en: is foolish, wicked and proud.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches not to judge alone, because only Hashem judges alone, and not to force others to accept your opinion.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do not judge alone,
because no one judges alone except the One.
And do not say: Accept my opinion,
because they are allowed to, and not you.
chunks.explain: The other judges, who are the majority, can decide.

summary: Rabbi Yonasan teaches that one who keeps the Torah when he is poor will in the end keep it when he is rich, and one who stops learning because he is rich will in the end stop because he is poor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yonasan says:
Whoever keeps the Torah when he is poor,
in the end will keep it when he is rich.
And whoever stops keeping the Torah because he is rich,
in the end will stop it because he is poor.

summary: Rabbi Meir teaches to do less business and more Torah, to be humble before everyone, and that Hashem has a big reward for anyone who works hard at Torah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
Do less business,
and be busy with Torah.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי שְׁפַל רוּחַ בִּפְנֵי כָל אָדָם.
chunks.en: And be humble before every person.
And if you stopped learning Torah,
you will have many things that stop you.
chunks.explain: One wasted moment leads to more.

chunks.en: And if you worked hard in Torah,

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ שָׂכָר הַרְבֵּה לִתֶּן לָךְ:
chunks.en: He has a lot of reward to give you.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov teaches that each mitzvah makes a friend who speaks up for us, and each aveirah makes an accuser. Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar teaches that a gathering for the sake of Heaven will last.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
One who does one mitzvah
gets for himself one defender.
chunks.explain: Someone who speaks up for him before Hashem.

chunks.en: And one who does one aveirah
gets for himself one accuser.
Teshuvah and good deeds
are like a shield against punishment.
Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says:
Every gathering that is for the sake of Heaven
will in the end last.
And one that is not for the sake of Heaven
will not last in the end.

summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua teaches to honor your student like yourself, your friend like your teacher, and your teacher like Hashem.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua says:

chunks.he: יְהִי כְבוֹד תַּלְמִידְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלְּךָ,
chunks.en: Let your student's honor be as dear to you as your own,
and your friend's honor like the respect for your teacher,
and the respect for your teacher like the fear of Heaven.

summary: Rabbi Yehudah teaches to be careful when you learn, because a mistake in learning can lead to doing wrong. Rabbi Shimon teaches that there are three crowns, but a good name is above them all.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
Be careful in your learning,
because a mistake in learning counts as doing it on purpose.
Rabbi Shimon says:
There are three crowns:

chunks.he: כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה וְכֶתֶר כְּהֻנָּה וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת,
chunks.en: the crown of Torah, and the crown of the Kohanim, and the crown of kingship,

chunks.he: וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן:
chunks.en: but the crown of a good name is above them all.

summary: Rabbi Nehorai teaches to go to a place of Torah, and not to think the Torah will come to you by itself or that you can understand it alone without friends.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nehorai says:
Move yourself to a place of Torah,
and do not say that it will come after you,
that your friends will make it last in your hand.
chunks.explain: You need friends to learn with.

chunks.en: And do not lean on your own understanding (Mishlei 3).

summary: Rabbi Yannai teaches that we cannot understand why wicked people may have it good and tzaddikim may suffer. Rabbi Masya teaches to greet everyone first and to be a tail to lions rather than a head to foxes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yannai says:
It is not in our hands to understand the calm of the wicked,
nor the sufferings of the tzaddikim.
Rabbi Masya ben Charash says:
Be the first to greet every person.
And be a tail to lions,
chunks.explain: Be the smallest among great people.

chunks.en: and do not be a head to foxes.

summary: Rabbi Yaakov teaches that this world is like a front hall before the World to Come. We should get ready here so we can enter the palace.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yaakov says:
This world is like a front hall
before the World to Come.
Get yourself ready in the front hall,
so that you can go into the palace.

summary: Rabbi Yaakov teaches that one hour of teshuvah and good deeds in this world is better than all of the World to Come, and one hour of calm in the World to Come is better than all of this world.

chunks.en: He used to say:
One hour of teshuvah
and good deeds in this world
is better than all the life of the World to Come.
And one hour of
calm of the spirit in the World to Come
is better than all the life of this world.

summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar teaches to choose the right time: don't try to calm a friend when he is angry, don't comfort him right after someone died, and don't look at him when he is embarrassed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

chunks.he: אַל תְּרַצֶּה אֶת חֲבֵרְךָ בִשְׁעַת כַּעֲסוֹ,
chunks.en: Do not try to calm your friend when he is angry,

chunks.he: וְאַל תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמֵּתוֹ מֻטָּל לְפָנָיו,
chunks.en: and do not comfort him while his dead relative is lying before him,
and do not ask him about his promise at the time he makes it,
chunks.explain: Wait until he can listen calmly.

chunks.en: and do not try to see him when he has done something wrong.

summary: Shmuel HaKatan teaches, using a pasuk, not to be happy when your enemy falls.

chunks.en: Shmuel HaKatan says:
(Mishlei 24) When your enemy falls, do not
be happy, and when he trips, let your heart not be glad,
or else Hashem will see, and it will be bad
in His eyes, and He will turn His anger away from him.

summary: Elisha ben Avuyah teaches that learning as a child stays strong, like ink on new paper. Rebbi teaches not to look at the container but at what is inside it.

chunks.en: Elisha ben Avuyah says:
One who learns as a child, what is he like?
Like ink written on new paper.
And one who learns as an old man, what is he like?
Like ink written on erased paper.
Rabbi Yosi bar Yehudah
of Kfar HaBavli says:

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מִן הַקְּטַנִּים לְמַה הוּא דוֹמֶה,
chunks.en: One who learns from young people, what is he like?

chunks.he: לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים קֵהוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן מִגִּתּוֹ.
chunks.en: Like one who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine straight from the press.

chunks.he: וְהַלּוֹמֵד מִן הַזְּקֵנִים לְמַה הוּא דוֹמֶה,
chunks.en: And one who learns from old people, what is he like?

chunks.he: לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים בְּשֵׁלוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן.
chunks.en: Like one who eats ripe grapes and drinks old wine.
Rebbi says:
Do not look at the jug,
but at what is inside it.
There is a new jug full of old wine,
and an old one that does not even have new wine in it.

summary: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar teaches that jealousy, wanting too much, and chasing honor take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says:
Jealousy, wanting too much, and chasing honor,
take a person out of the world.

summary: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar teaches that Hashem made us and will judge us fairly, with no forgetting and no bribes. We should not think we can escape by dying, because everything happens by Hashem's will.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Those who are born will die,
and the dead will come back to life,
and those who live will be judged.
To know, to tell others, and to make it known that He is G-d,
He is the One Who forms,
He is the Creator,
He is the One Who understands,
He is the Judge,
He is the Witness,
He is the One Who brings the case,
and He will one day judge.
Blessed is He,
that before Him there is no wrongdoing,
and no forgetting,
and no favoring anyone,
and no taking bribes,
because everything is His.
And know that everything goes by the account.
And do not let your yetzer hara promise you that the grave
is a place to escape to.
Because against your will you are formed,
and against your will you are born,
and against your will you live,
and against your will you die,
and against your will you will one day give
a judgment and an accounting before the King of all
kings, the Holy One, blessed is He.
